findings.title: Eager dynamic imports of all apps can cause unhandled rejections and needless loading
findings.body: The appStore object calls import('./...') for every integration as soon as this module is evaluated. Any import of appStore therefore starts loading all app bundles, even if only one app is needed. It also creates promises that may never be awaited; if one dynamic import or module evaluation rejects, Node/Next can observe an unhandled promise rejection. A lazy cached loader per app or explicit catch/handling would avoid both the startup cost and crash risk.

findings.title: Async forEach is not awaited when deleting recurring calendar events
findings.body: Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for async callbacks. In the recurring cancellation path, getCalendar and deleteEvent are awaited inside the callback, and only the resolved delete result is later pushed into apiDeletes. The later Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) can therefore run before these operations are finished or before anything is pushed. External calendar deletions may not complete before the response, and rejections are unhandled. Use Promise.all(credentials.map(...)) and collect the deletion promises.

findings.title: `await apiDeletes` does not wait for the queued integration deletions
findings.body: apiDeletes is an array of promises/values, but `await apiDeletes` awaits the array itself, not its elements. In the paid cancellation branch the handler continues immediately, so external calendar/video deletions are not awaited and any rejection becomes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` if these operations should be awaited.

findings.title: Reschedule deletion loop uses async forEach without awaiting
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts calendar/video deletion but forEach ignores the returned promises. The surrounding try/catch only catches synchronous errors, so failures from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting are not handled. Reschedule returns true and sends the reschedule email before the old events are reliably removed. Use Promise.all over the refs and await/handle the results.

The surrounding try/catch only catches synchronous errors, so failures from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting are not handled. Reschedule returns true and sends the reschedule email before the old events are reliably removed. Use Promise.all over the refs and await/handle the results.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: The requestReschedule mutation iterates refs with forEach(async ...) and then sends the reschedule email and returns. The async deletions are not awaited and have no catch, so old calendar/video events may remain and rejections become unhandled. Await Promise.all of the deletion operations and handle/log errors.

findings.title: One failing calendar import can reject all availability results
findings.body: getCachedResults uses Promise.all over getCalendar calls. getCalendar now awaits dynamic app imports, so a rejected import or initialization error for one credential rejects the whole Promise.all and makes availability fail for all calendars. Consider Promise.allSettled or a per-credential catch that returns null/empty for the failing calendar.

findings.title: Video adapter loading failures bypass the Cal Video fallback
findings.body: createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters before the try/catch that implements the Cal Video fallback. Since getVideoAdapters now awaits dynamic imports, a rejected import for the selected video app will throw before the try block, so the intended fallback to Cal Video never runs. Wrap adapter resolution in the try/catch or handle import failures explicitly.

findings.title: Video adapters are loaded sequentially
findings.body: getVideoAdapters awaits each appStore dynamic import inside a for...of loop. When multiple credentials are supplied, module loading is serialized even though the imports are independent. Use Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...)) to load adapters in parallel.

findings.title: Warning logs the module object instead of the app identifier
findings.body: The warning interpolates paymentApp, which is the resolved module namespace or undefined, so it prints [object Module]/undefined rather than the missing app identifier. Log paymentAppCredentials.app?.dirName or appId to make the warning actionable. The same pattern exists in other payment-app lookups.
